notes: resolvePulseScale computes (widthPx - PULSE_DIAMETER_MARGIN_PX)/imageWidth (fit-to-width), but line 37 then multiplies by variance.sizeMultiplier * 3, so blobs render ~3x vein width and the margin subtraction is cosmetic. Name/margin genuinely misrepresent runtime; behavior itself is not buggy.
lastIntensity01 is seeded (veinsEdgeState.ts:37) and reassigned (veinsEdgeTick.ts:117) but grep finds no reader in non-test code; it is write-only dead state that influences no rendering.

Observation is technically true (color:'#ffffff' is a tintable placeholder; real color comes from setTint(variance.tint) in spawnPulse), but a white base for a tinted texture is a standard idiom with no behavioral or realistic misread risk.

ropeSignature payload includes timeMs and pulseValue (cycleProgressVisual.ts:44-45), which change every animated frame, so the lastSignature guard almost never matches during play; the cache appears to skip re-sync but buys nothing except when the node is paused/static.

grep confirms countBlobsThatFitSourceGap and resolveBlobSpacing have no non-test caller; live spawn logic in veinsPulseTick.ts computes spacing/gap inline, so these tested exports are a parallel/abandoned implementation that green tests make look load-bearing.

blend:1 (glow/eyes) and blend:0 (silhouette) are passed as bare numbers via setBlendMode(style.blend as Phaser.BlendModes); per blendModes.ts these are ADD=1/NORMAL=0. Behavior is correct but the named constants are bypassed with magic numbers that read as arbitrary flags.

resolveBlink returns eye OPENNESS: 1 when window>durationMs (not blinking), dipping toward 0 at the blink midpoint, and is consumed as openness=Math.max(0.04, blink). The name is inverted relative to the value it returns.

normalizeThickness returns 0 for the ignore-set shapes, that 0 is baked into the cache key (lines 49-55) so different requested thicknesses share one texture, and the draw call falls back to thickness||10. Correct for shapes that ignore stroke width, but the name hides that thickness is discarded.

resolveGlyphPlacementColor returns paletteColor || placement.colorHex, so a palette key that resolves to an empty string (or any falsy value) is silently treated as absent and falls through to colorHex even though the palette key is present.

Only GLYPH_TEXTURE_SIZE is imported (by GlyphTextureGen.ts:5); grep finds no consumer of drawCircle/drawRing/drawHexRing/drawOctRing/drawSquareRing/drawPixel. Live ring rendering is elsewhere, so the module name and exported draw fns misrepresent what is used.

assertAvatarAppearance only checks appearance.appearanceKey is truthy and throws otherwise; every other field (indices, scales, blink timing) is unvalidated, so a malformed appearance with a set key passes the 'assert'.

validateScratchSlots collects leaked slot names and only console.errors; it does not clear or destroy the leaked objects, so the leak proceeds and anchors are released regardless. The 'validate' name implies blocking it does not do.
setScratchAlpha sets alpha on exactly one object ((backgroundImage ?? root)), leaving the other anchors untouched; the name reads as if it dims the whole instance.

readNonEmptyString tests value.trim() for emptiness but returns the ORIGINAL untrimmed value, so ' abc ' is returned with its whitespace; trimming only happens later in AvatarAppearanceRegistry.resolve.

acquire runs (acquireFn ?? resetFn); DisplayTypePool always supplies acquire=activatePooledObject, which only re-adds to the scene and does NOT call resetFn, so reused objects are reset only on release. The resetFn-in-acquire fallback never fires for the real pools.

resolveNervousDeliveredRate ignores all three underscore-prefixed params and returns 0; it is called at veinFlowProjection.ts:41 to set edge.deliveredRate for every nervous edge, so nervous edges get deliveredRate=0. It is a permanent stub typed as a computation.

resolveDemandWidth (and the resolvePulsedWidth it wraps) have no caller anywhere; demand edges get width from resolveThrottleWidth in veinsDisplayBuilder.ts:38, which ignores sourceRadius/drawFraction. The doc comment's 'consistent structural logic as supply edges' describes dead code.

The try/catch at getImageUrl guards only the synchronous resolveDisplayImageSpec + buildDisplayCacheKey; the render runs later inside resolveCached's Promise.resolve().then(...), whose own error handler (line 86) rejects render failures. The outer catch is dead for render-time throws.

The module-level registry IS distinct from the scene registry, but the load-bearing claim (cache never cleared, unbounded across the tab) is contradicted: AvatarAppearanceRegistry.resolve caches by seed and syncEpoch clears the whole cache on epoch change, and buildBodyAvatarImageRequest calls syncEpoch(seed) before resolve. Within an epoch it is bounded by distinct subjects.

When scene.textureManager is undefined, getGlyphTexture is undefined and textureKey ?? '' yields ''; Phaser TextureManager.get('') returns the __MISSING placeholder (verified in phaser source), which has a source image, so readPhaserTextureSource does not throw and the checkerboard is painted. Contingent on an undefined textureManager.

LINEAR_FILTER is the string 'LINEAR' cast to FilterMode, but the enum LINEAR is 0; Phaser WebGLRenderer.setTextureFilter uses (filter === 0) ? LINEAR : NEAREST (verified in source), so the string fails strict-equals and the strip is filtered NEAREST. Sibling files use the real enum. Visual impact on a solid strip is negligible but the name asserts the opposite of runtime.

main() never references uResolution or uCameraZoom (confirmed in the GLSL), yet applyBiologicalFogUniforms sets both (lines 27,33) and the resize handler re-pushes uResolution (BiologicalFogBackground.ts:92-93). The GLSL compiler strips unused uniforms, so those setUniform calls are no-ops against nonexistent locations.

_textureManager and _scene are accepted but never referenced in the body; presentation is built purely from the registry appearance and canvas. The signature advertises a scene/texture dependency the code does not have.

createNodeOverlayDisplayBoundsFromRadius returns null when radius <= 0 (nodeOverlayDisplayBounds.ts:47), and the `if (bounds)` guard at line 55 leaves scratch.nodeOverlayDisplayBounds pointing at the previous frame's bounds. TransferModule.ts:65 assigns unconditionally (radius clamped to MIN), so this module is the inconsistent one and can retain stale bounds when the glyph shrinks out of view.

getPerm memoizes a 512-byte Uint8Array per distinct seed in a module-level Map that is never cleared or capped (line 36). Over a long session with many distinct vein seeds this accumulates for the life of the module; a slow, bounded-by-seed-count leak.

advanceWavePhase decrements state.wavePhaseRad every frame with no modulo/wrap (lines 13-20), so magnitude grows unbounded for long-lived nervous veins and eventually loses float precision when fed to Math.sin. The forced per-frame recompute is largely inherent to animation; the precision degradation is real but only at extreme runtimes.

Inside while(spawnCarry >= 1), the `const pulse = state.pulses.at(-1); if (!pulse) continue;` path loops back without decrementing spawnCarry or advancing the ordinal. It is safe only because spawnPulse unconditionally pushes (veinsPulseLifecycle.ts:42); if spawnPulse ever early-returns this becomes an infinite loop. Latent, does not manifest today.

readProducerResource scores state entries (restricted to keys in PRODUCER_LIGHTS) by ad-hoc shape heuristics (allowWithdraw/allowDeposit/visible/max), and ties resolve to the first-seen key via strict > and Object.entries order. Any change to state-entry shape could silently reassign the resource color; latent coupling risk, only bites when multiple producer keys coexist.

On active distress the tick force-shows scratch.root and repositions/shows overlayAnchor (lines 89-91), but hideHalos() only kills tweens and hides the three halo images; it never restores overlayAnchor visibility/position or root visibility, so distress state can leak into later frames after recovery or loss of target.

createProgressBarSlots hardcodes Array.from({length:4}) while progressBarTick.ts:34-35 iterates RESOURCE_PROGRESS_BAR_POSITIONS (currently 4) and indexes slots[index] with no undefined guard. The count invariant is unenforced: a 5th position makes slots[4] undefined and hideProgressBarSlot(undefined) throws. Latent, requires editing the constant.

The NaN premise is contradicted by the Zod schema: glyphs.ts validates position with z.number().int().min(0).max(8) and delayMsByPosition with z.array(...).length(9), so position 0..8 always indexes into a length-9 array for schema-valid cartridges. The TS type number[] looks loose but the runtime schema guarantees the length, so the out-of-bounds/NaN path cannot occur.

destroy() calls runtime.destroy (glyphModuleRuntime.destroyGlyphImages sets scratch.mainImage=null) then unconditionally reassigns dCtx.scratch.mainImage = preservedMain (line 44). If the AvatarModule that owned that silhouette was already destroyed and released it to the pool, this writes a stale/released reference back, defeating the null-out; order-dependent dangling reference.

The star6 core case calls starPoints(3, outer) with inner radius equal to outer (so points are not a true star) and mirrors the second triangle with `128 - point.y + 10`, an asymmetric +10px offset. Since star6 is in normalizeThickness's ignore-set and the core path is tried first (returns true), this asymmetric texture is what actually renders.

grep finds no importer of glyphShapeDrawFns.ts and only GLYPH_TEXTURE_SIZE imported from glyphShapeDrawFnsRings.ts. These define an alternate shape set (e.g. drawStar6 as a symmetric Star of David, T=10) that renders nothing; they present as the shape source of truth but are dead and diverge from the live core/stroke paths.
